source_context: The user asked GPT-6 to attack another useful original-to-the-library theorem following LeanFrontier rules and same full upstream workflow. After auditing upstream CONTRACT.md, open PRs, Mathlib release policy (v4.35.0) and relevant pinned Mathlib modules, GPT-6 selected the classical bounded eventual-periodicity theorem for arbitrary finite self-maps, plus uniform factorial stabilization of their iterations. Mathlib has pigeonhole lemmas and periodic-point machinery, including an injective-map periodicity theorem, but searches found no equivalent bounded transient-plus-period interface nor this uniform transformation-monoid exponent statement. GPT-6 produced the Lean statements and proofs independently; the human gave no formal statement. Pigeonhole yields collision among the first card+1 iterates; the collision implies eventual periodicity with tail length plus period ≤ card, and factorial divisibility yields a uniform power identity.
